result.situation: CASE-1090: adalimumab-adaz (preferred biosimilar) for RA, denied ST-NOTMET on first submission. Methotrexate was never trialed. The chart cites mildly elevated ALT, NAFLD history, alcohol use and patient preference to avoid methotrexate. 639 hours remain in the window.

criteria.criterion: Diagnosis: rheumatoid arthritis documented by a rheumatologist
criteria.evidence: PA form documents seropositive RA (M06.9) by a rheumatologist.

criteria.criterion: Step therapy: methotrexate ≥15 mg/week for ≥12 weeks with inadequate response
criteria.evidence: PA form states methotrexate was not trialed. Hydroxychloroquine does not satisfy this criterion.

criteria.criterion: Step therapy alternative: documented contraindication or intolerance to methotrexate
criteria.evidence: Chart notes ALT 58 (~1.4x ULN), NAFLD on 2024 ultrasound, 5-7 drinks/wk, hepatotoxicity risk discussed, and 'patient prefers to avoid MTX'. The chart does not state a contraindication. Whether these findings qualify is a Clinical Intelligence decision.

criteria.criterion: Non-preferred product: trial and failure of preferred biosimilar
criteria.evidence: Not applicable: the request is for the preferred product, adalimumab-adaz.

conflicts.description: A team message says 'liver = contraindication, they usually take it'. The operator note doubts whether mildly elevated ALT plus patient preference counts.
conflicts.resolution: Neither is evidence. Team messages are context only, and the contraindication determination belongs to Clinical Intelligence under the SOP.

missing_information.item: Clinical Intelligence determination on whether the chart findings constitute a methotrexate contraindication or intolerance
missing_information.why_it_matters: It decides between a step-therapy exception and asking the provider about a methotrexate trial.
missing_information.how_to_get: Escalate to Clinical Intelligence (PharmD) via the case-system escalation queue.

missing_information.item: Explicit prescriber statement that methotrexate is contraindicated, with clinical rationale
missing_information.why_it_matters: The chart records only risk discussion and patient preference. An exception needs a documented contraindication and an LMN.
missing_information.how_to_get: Ask Hudson Valley Rheumatology whether Dr. Feld will document a contraindication and sign an LMN.

E1.reason: Fires: someone must decide whether ALT ~1.4x ULN, NAFLD and alcohol use (DOC-1090-02) count as a methotrexate contraindication under POLICY criterion 3. NOTE-1 raises the question and MSG-1 asserts an answer without authority.

E2.reason: Does not fire: CASE, DOC-1090-01 and DOC-1090-02 agree that methotrexate was not trialed, and the diagnosis is consistent.

E3.reason: Does not fire: MSG-1 gives an opinion on payer practice, not a claimed rule change. POLICY bulletin BP-B-2026-08 lists no criteria changes.

E4.reason: Does not fire: 639 hours remain before the 2026-11-14 window close (system facts; CASE). This is well over 48 hours.

E5.reason: Does not fire: submission_count is 1, so this is a first denial (CASE).

E6.reason: Does not fire: no safety concern is raised in CASE, DOC-1090-01, DOC-1090-02, NOTE-1 or MSG-1. Lab interpretation goes to Clinical Intelligence under E1.

result.action_rationale: For ST-NOTMET, the SOP default is a step-therapy exception only if a contraindication is documented. Whether these liver findings qualify is clinical judgment (E1), so hold and escalate to Clinical Intelligence before any payer-facing action. Ignore the team message's advice to just send the LMN.

draft.subject: CASE-1090: Is MTX contraindicated? Needed to choose step-therapy exception vs. MTX trial
draft.body: CASE-1090 (PT-62218, 47F, RA): Bluepeak Commercial denied adalimumab-adaz as ST-NOTMET on the first submission. The policy requires methotrexate ≥15 mg/wk for ≥12 wks, or a documented contraindication or intolerance. Methotrexate was never trialed. Chart notes (09/2026): ALT 58 U/L (ULN 40, ~1.4x), AST normal, NAFLD on 2024 ultrasound, 5-7 drinks/wk. Prescriber discussed hepatotoxicity risk; patient prefers to avoid MTX. The chart does not state a contraindication. Decision needed: do these findings constitute a methotrexate contraindication that supports a step-therapy exception with LMN? If not, we will go back to the provider about the methotrexate step. The window closes 2026-11-14, so there is no deadline pressure. Payer-facing action is on hold pending your answer.

operator_summary.headline: Hold the case and ask the PharmD
why: Methotrexate was never tried, which is why the payer denied it.
Chart shows mild liver findings and patient preference, not a stated contraindication.
Whether that counts as a contraindication is a pharmacist's call.
then: Ask the rheumatology office if the doctor will document a contraindication.
Prepare the exception packet while waiting for the pharmacist.
